# FFmpeg source and build references for VYRE Audio 2.1.1

This package contains **third-party source only**, not VYRE's proprietary application source. VYRE Audio 2.1.1 distributes Electron 45.5.0's shared FFmpeg libraries. FFmpeg's LGPL 2.1-or-later text is provided in `FFmpeg-COPYING.LGPLv2.1` and `LGPL-2.1.txt`; the Chromium FFmpeg fork's `LICENSE.md` and `CREDITS.chromium` are also supplied. These files contain additional component notices and terms.

## Contents and source provenance

- `ffmpeg-chromium-9db86ce5.tar.gz`: complete upstream Chromium FFmpeg fork checkout at `9db86ce5b5b454dfc96c435f9f0723012980c37f`, including Chromium's existing modifications, FFmpeg source, `BUILD.gn`, `ffmpeg_generated.gni`, `ffmpeg_options.gni`, build scripts and generated per-platform configurations. Upstream: <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/third_party/ffmpeg/+/9db86ce5b5b454dfc96c435f9f0723012980c37f>.
- `electron-v45.5.0-source.tar.gz`: the upstream Electron 45.5.0 source tag, including its `DEPS`, all `patches/ffmpeg`, the Chromium patches, build profiles under `build/args`, build workflows and `docs/development/build-instructions-gn.md`. Upstream: <https://github.com/electron/electron/tree/v45.5.0>.
- `ffmpeg-9db86ce5-electron-45.5.0-patched.tar.gz`: the above FFmpeg checkout after applying Electron's five `patches/ffmpeg` patches in the exact order in `electron-45.5.0/patches/ffmpeg/.patches`. All five patches applied cleanly to the original checkout. The patched archive is a convenience copy; the upstream archive and original patches are retained separately for verification.
- `chromium-156.0.8078.109-DEPS`, `chromium-156.0.8078.109-build.tar.gz`, `chromium-156.0.8078.109-media-ffmpeg.tar.gz`, `chromium-156.0.8078.109-generate-stubs.tar.gz` and `chromium-156.0.8078.109-LICENSE`: the exact Chromium tag's dependency manifest and selected build and FFmpeg-related script directories. Archive contents are rooted at their named Chromium subdirectories (`build/`, `media/ffmpeg/`, `tools/generate_stubs/`). The complete Chromium source and other pinned dependencies are available through <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/156.0.8078.109> and the provided DEPS manifest.
- `chromium-156.0.8078.109-opus.tar.gz`: Chromium-tagged `third_party/opus`, including Opus source and notices, a dependency referenced by the FFmpeg build.
- `chromium-nasm-525a09a8.tar.gz`: NASM source at the revision in Chromium DEPS, used for x64 assembly. Its contents are rooted at `third_party/nasm/`.
- `electron-v45.5.0-SHASUMS256.txt`: Electron's published checksums for its release files. They can be used to check the official Electron runtime ZIPs; see <https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v45.5.0>.

Electron's DEPS pins Chromium `156.0.8078.109`; that Chromium DEPS pins FFmpeg `9db86ce5b5b454dfc96c435f9f0723012980c37f`. Electron's `patches/config.json` applies the separate FFmpeg patch series. Its `build/args/release.gn` selects a shared FFmpeg library, and `build/args/all.gn` sets `ffmpeg_branding = "Chrome"` and `proprietary_codecs = true`. The corresponding checked-in `chromium/config/Chrome/{win/x64,mac/arm64,linux/x64,linux/arm64}` files specify `CONFIG_GPL=0`, `CONFIG_NONFREE=0`, and H.264/AAC decoders enabled. These are source/build-configuration observations; an independent reproduction of Electron's complete release build and final per-platform GN arguments was not performed. Electron's separate `build/args/ffmpeg.gn` configures the alternate Chromium-branded library and is not evidence that VYRE uses that alternate build.

To reconstruct the original source state, extract the Chromium FFmpeg archive into `src/third_party/ffmpeg`, extract Electron at `src/electron`, and apply the listed patches in `.patches` order. The patched archive provides the same FFmpeg source state directly. For a complete rebuild, follow Electron's tagged GN build instructions and obtain the remaining Chromium source, its DEPS-pinned dependencies, applicable Electron Chromium patches, toolchains, SDKs and platform-specific build prerequisites. The selected Chromium subdirectory archives in this package are not a complete Chromium checkout. A bit-for-bit rebuild or an ABI-compatible modified library was not produced or tested here.

## Binary comparison

The official Electron runtime ZIPs cached for all four targets matched Electron's published SHA-256 checksums. The extracted Windows `ffmpeg.dll` (`db2b0471b18b5a6c1fd8bc4041f25b1056fa7d86c884d4f14d5a04d3f8d0dbd0`), Linux x64 `libffmpeg.so` (`5b84456c27fdaf126845e5a40455512630e64cde153aef0ec2dd1c4656f80c61`) and Linux ARM64 `libffmpeg.so` (`f786237a9951d694b76cdeac47d7861ae0b7c80966b3207ed8fcd0b8dd19e87e`) were byte-identical to the corresponding files extracted from the final VYRE artifacts.

The official macOS dylib and the VYRE DMG dylib have different signatures. After removing their signatures from temporary copies, their file lengths matched and only two bytes differed, within the Mach-O `__LINKEDIT` virtual-size field (`0x20000` versus `0x1c000`). This establishes a very close match consistent with the packaging/signing step, but is not a claim of byte-identical signed files. VYRE's signed dylib SHA-256 is `631344c6cc6db3a9ab972af082e0025bdddd4bb9f6074f13b82ed87a12fde1cb`.

## Replacement and user rights

FFmpeg is distributed separately as a shared library. The Linux x64 and ARM64 executables declare `libffmpeg.so` as a needed library; the macOS Electron Framework references `@rpath/libffmpeg.dylib`; Windows includes a separate `ffmpeg.dll` and the application binary references that filename. Replacement must be ABI-compatible and preserve expected exports and architecture. No functional execution using a modified library was performed on Windows, Linux or macOS.

On macOS, replacing the dylib invalidates the existing app signature. In a temporary copy, replacing it with the original Electron dylib made signature verification fail; ad-hoc re-signing the dylib, enclosing Electron Framework and app made `codesign --verify --deep --strict` succeed, preserving the app's `disable-library-validation` entitlement. This verifies the signature mechanics only, not execution or the behavior of arbitrary modified libraries. Re-signing a user's copy can require appropriate platform tools and may affect Gatekeeper trust; no developer account is needed for ad-hoc signing.

The LGPL conditions concerning a user's own modifications and reverse engineering for debugging those modifications must not be overridden by VYRE's proprietary terms. See the adjacent VYRE license notice. Providing a source archive and documenting a shared library does not by itself prove that every applicable corresponding-source, relinking or codec/patent condition is fulfilled. In particular, the full generated release build arguments and a functional replacement on each target have not been independently verified.
